text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where team members frequently merge their code changes into a shared main repository. Instead of waiting for a big release day, every change triggers an automated process known as a CI pipeline. This pipeline automatically builds the software and runs a full suite of tests, such as unit and integration tests. The main goal is to catch issues early, ideally within minutes of a change being submitted. If a test fails, the team is immediately alerted and can fix the problem before it grows. As a result, CI helps reduce bugs, improves code quality, and makes the entire development process much smoother and more reliable.
